doc.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Parents from Italy and the eight Balassoni children
summary: He names his Italian-born parents, their birthplaces, his half-sisters from his father's first marriage, and his brothers and sisters.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Let’s back up. Could you tell us your parents’ full names?
My dad is Louis, Sr. My mother’s name was Carmen. That’s the American name, Carmen.
Do you remember their Italian names?
Yes. My dad was Louis Balassoni. My mother was Carmen Bartolucci.
Bartolucci?
Bartolucci.
Do you know where they were from in Italy?
My father was born in Naples. My mother was born in Milano. So I’m half Milanese and half Napolitan.
Are they both first generation or second generation in America?
Second, I think?
So they were born in America?

Yeah. No, they’re first generation, born in Italy. They came over. Our family – we had eight children, four girls and four boys. The girls came first. Four of the girls were my mother’s sister’s. Have I got that right?
Francine, do you want to make an editorial comment here?
Dad was married to my mother’s sister.
Why don’t you stop. Let’s get some clarity.
[recording interrupted]
Louie, if you could tell us about your siblings. Tell us about your early family recollections.

There were eight children altogether. All the girls came first, and then the boys came second. But the first three girls were from my dad’s first marriage to his wife who came from Italy with him. Those three girls – his wife passed away, so my dad sent to Italy for the sister. When the sister came to America, they had five children: one girl and four boys. So actually Josephine, Dee Dee, and Edie are my half-sisters. Mary is my full sister. And of course the four boys.
Do you remember the names of your brothers?

Yes. The oldest brother was Frank. He passed away. The oldest girl was Edie. She passed away. The rest of us are still around. That’s Tony. He’s younger than me. Henry is the baby of the boys. Josephine, Dee Dee, and Mary are the girls left.
